citation.title: Ion Thermal Transport in the H-mode Edge Transport Barrier on DIII-D
citation.authors: S. R. Haskey, A. Ashourvan, S. Banerjee, K. Barada, E. A. Belli, A. Bortolon, J. Candy, J. Chen, C. Chrystal, B. A. Grierson, R. J. Groebner, F. M. Laggner, M. Knolker, G. J. Kramer, M. R. Major, G. Mckee, G. M. Staebler, Z. Yan, M. A. Van Zeeland
citation.venue: Physics of Plasmas (inferred from accepted-manuscript notice; verify)
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1063/5.0072155 (stated on the manuscript's own 'please cite' line, not taken from the reference list)

topic: Main-ion versus C6+ impurity CER temperature in the DIII-D pedestal and its effect on ion and electron power balance
own_question: How does pedestal ion heat flux vary with ion collisionality, and is it neoclassical or turbulent?
actual_method_and_evidence: Offline analysis of three DIII-D discharges. The authors used inter-ELM-filtered profiles (80-95% of the ELM cycle) and direct main-ion (MICER) temperature measurements. The analysis combined TRANSP power balance, NEO, nonlinear CGYRO at a single radius, TGLF, and BES/DBS/RIP fluctuation measurements. Appendix A uses a different shot to compare D+ and C6+ temperatures.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Reported C6+ CES temperature in the pedestal is a conventional measurement label, and it can depart from main-ion temperature toward the separatrix on DIII-D.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: Appendix A, pp.12-13; Sec. III A, p.5
claim_checks.qualification: DIII-D only. The divergence is not fully understood. Applying a Zeeman/fine-structure correction reduces the core offset. This does not establish anything about KSTAR.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Edge ion-electron exchange is sensitive to the temperature difference between species, so the choice of ion temperature affects inferred channel heat fluxes.
claim_checks.qualification: This is a power-balance sensitivity on DIII-D, not a nowcasting result.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable. All processing is offline and time-window averaged, with no real-time or report-timing content.
validation_if_relevant: Model-to-experiment comparison on three discharges. There are no held-out data.
forbidden_inferences: That impurity CES temperature equals ion temperature or physical truth
That KSTAR shows the same C6+/D+ divergence
That BES fluctuations predict Ti or CES reports
That this work involves causal or real-time estimation
Collisionality or turbulence conclusions applied to our chord
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include as a single background citation qualifying that our carbon CES target is a reported impurity temperature rather than main-ion truth. It also gives context that BES sees pedestal ion-scale fluctuations. It is not methodological precedent for our work.
